answer: Each agent must post a bond from a scarce, externally costly resource before it can claim rewards, and the bond stays locked while its actions are challenged. A protocol can slash it when an onyx reputation record shows coordinated fraud, using a cipher-signed audit trail to link claims to the deposit without exposing private data. Spawning a tide of fake identities therefore does not multiply influence for free: the attacker must lock more capital per identity and risks losing it.
